review_scope: Independent text/AST review of root trainer snapshot and its input/adapter/suite interfaces; no model or scientific data execution.

findings.problem: The final stream_hash_algorithm prose differed from R63 while the then-current saved-record audit required literal equality, causing a deterministic endpoint audit failure.
findings.fix: Final driver copies the bound historical description. Revised audit requires nonempty wording while keeping all original seven actual chains and final states exact.

findings.problem: Recovery rejected a committed step 50000 and rejected an existing partial FINAL_FLOW output, so a failure after the last checkpoint could not finish the same endpoint.
findings.fix: Accept committed_update <= 50000. The loop is empty at 50000; logs/model can be restored for finalization. Existing finalization outputs require byte-identical native_attempts archives before replacement; NPZ and torch outputs use fsync temporary-file/atomic replacement.

findings.problem: Checkpoint creator was required to equal the immediately preceding attempt. A second crash before a new checkpoint would prevent another resume from the earlier valid creator.
findings.fix: Checkpoint creator and immediately previous physical attempt are checked separately; creator must occur in preserved attempts. A recovery edge uses the actual current OWNED_SCIENCE_NONCE.

findings.problem: A completed Adam call can precede logical log commit. Old audit equality would reject honest preserved crash work or induce undercounting.
findings.fix: Physical new_response_updates means known Adam calls and records their nonnegative difference from the committed interval as known_uncommitted_optimizer_steps. Revised audit accepts that explicit difference, verifies prior operation lower bounds, and retains exact uninterrupted totals.

findings.problem: Checkpoint metadata had no digest published at creation. A recovery request hashing the post-crash cache could not establish equality to the originally committed bytes.
findings.fix: Write/fsync temporary checkpoint, compute its digest, durably publish PENDING receipt, atomically replace/fsync cache directory, then durably publish COMMITTED receipt. Recovery verifies a named published receipt/hash plus cache/hash, step, creator, and frozen bindings before deserialization.

findings.problem: The intermediate repair set restored updates before attempt_start_update. A later restore-validation failure could record negative known_uncommitted_optimizer_steps with zero new Adam calls.
findings.fix: Immediately after setting restored updates, initialize attempt_start_update, last_checkpoint_update, and current_update to that boundary before later assertions.

limitations: Static review cannot establish actual CUDA replay, full objective/parameter/Adam equivalence, resource use, runtime success, or scientific acceptance.
The guarded server artificial suite is still required before scientific TRAIN decode; existing numerical and A-F gates remain required afterward.
Recovery fixes were checked by code-path reasoning only. No native checkpoint was loaded and no crash/fault injection was performed.
The root worker owns recovery-request creation, preserved attempt evidence, PID-death proof, native exit receipts, deployment binding, and actual resource enforcement.
Verdict is limited to the bound snapshots. Subsequent source/config edits require renewed review of the changed paths.
